5.2.title: Response to Violence and Aggression Procedure
5.2.text:
5.2.1. Verbal Abuse
Where verbal abuse occurs:

• Employees should attempt to de-escalate the situation where it is safe to do so
• The individual may be referred to the relevant client where appropriate, and
• Where behaviour continues or escalates, Employees must assess whether it is safe to
continue work.

Where verbal abuse persists or escalates, work must cease and the situation escalated to a
Leader.
5.2.2. Property Damage
Where property damage occurs, including damage to vehicles, equipment, or signage:

• Employees must avoid confrontation and prioritise personal safety
• Police must be contacted where there is a threat to safety, and
• Leaders must determine whether work can safely continue.
5.2.3. Intimidation Involving Vehicles or Objects
Where intimidation occurs, including swerving, attempted impact, or objects being thrown:

• Employees must remain in the vehicle where safe to do so
• Police must be contacted immediately, and
• The incident must be escalated and work activities reassessed.
5.2.4. Physical Assault or Threats
Where a physical assault or credible threat occurs, including the presence of a weapon:

• Police must be contacted immediately
• Work activities must cease, and

• Employees must withdraw to a safe location.

Work must not resume until it has been determined that it is safe to do so.
5.2.5. Non-Verbal Intimidation
Non-verbal intimidation, including threatening gestures or behaviour intended to instill fear,
must be treated as a potential escalation risk. Where behaviour suggests an imminent
threat:

• Police must be contacted, and
• Work activities must cease.

5.1.title: Public Interaction Risk Management Procedure
5.1.text:
Violence and aggression risks must be managed using a risk-based approach, consistent
with Verra Mobility’s Risk Management Procedure.

This includes:

• Identifying situations where interaction with the public may present a risk
• Assessing the likelihood and potential severity of harm
• Implementing controls to eliminate or minimise risk, and
• Consulting with Employees when identifying risks and controls.

Prior to work commencing onsite, risks must be documented, assessed and mitigated using
Take 5 Form (IMS.03.00.FRM.02).

5.4.title: Welfare Support Procedure
5.4.text:
Where a Employee is involved in a violent or aggressive incident, Leaders must ensure
appropriate welfare support is provided. This may include:

• Medical assessment
• Access to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
• Temporary modification of duties, and / or
• Arranging safe transport home where required.

4.1.2.title: Verra Mobility Employees
4.1.2.text:
Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Remove themselves from situations where there is an immediate threat to safety.

4.2.1.title: Verra Mobility Employees
4.2.1.text:
Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Complete the Public Interaction Training Module (IMS.03.19.TRN.01) annually.

4.2.title: Competency Requirements
4.2.text:
4.2.1. Verra Mobility Employees
Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Complete the Public Interaction Training Module (IMS.03.19.TRN.01) annually.

5.5.title: Incident Hazards, Near Miss Reporting Procedure
5.5.text:
All Incidents, Near Misses and Hazards shall be reported as per Incident, Near Miss and
Hazard Management Procedure (IMS.06.01.PRO.01).

5.3.title: Decision to Continue Work Procedure
5.3.text:
Following any incident involving violence or aggression, a decision to continue work must
consider:

• Whether it is safe to continue
• Whether there is an ongoing risk to personal safety
• Whether property damage affects safe operation, and
• The physical and psychological condition of the Employee involved.

The welfare of the Employee must be the primary consideration

4.1.title: Specific Roles and Responsibilities Related to this Procedure
4.1.text:
4.1.1. Leaders
All Leaders are responsible for:

• Ensuring violence and aggression risks associated with their activities or contracts are
assessed and controlled
• Supporting Employees to remove themselves from unsafe situations
• Determining whether work activities can safely continue following an incident, and
• Ensuring incidents are reported and appropriate welfare support is provided.
4.1.2. Verra Mobility Employees
Verra Mobility Employees are required to:

• Remove themselves from situations where there is an immediate threat to safety.
